item.title: A multispecies foundation model for genome function prediction, gene annotation and sequence design
item.abstract: Comparative genomics and synthetic biology require models that can interpret, annotate, and design DNA sequences across species, yet genomic models have not combined these capabilities beyond a few well-characterized organisms. Here we introduce Nucleotide Transformer v3 (NTv3), a long-context cross-kingdom foundation model that provides a common backbone for functional prediction, gene annotation and controllable sequence generation across phylogenetically diverse species. NTv3 is pre-trained on more than 128,000 genomes using sequences up to 1Mb and post-trained on 16,262 functional tracks across 15 animal and plant genomes. NTv3 performs comparably to AlphaGenome on matched human assays and matches or exceeds evaluated published models for functional-track prediction across 19 species spanning mammals, birds, fish, plants, fungi and protists. Ablation experiments show that both genome pre-training and expanding functional supervision from human and mouse to 15 species improve track prediction. Leveraging these learned functional representations, NTv3 outperforms leading ab initio gene predictors across mammals, plants and insects, with fewer spurious gene models and improved recovery and reduced fragmentation of long genes. Finally, the same representations can be used with discrete diffusion to design regulatory DNA sequences with specific activity levels. We demonstrate this in plant and fly promoters and enhancers, and experimentally validate the activity and promoter selectivity of the generated fly enhancers. Together, NTv3 unifies genome interpretation, gene annotation and regulatory sequence design across the animal and plant kingdoms, with direct relevance to agriculture, biodiversity research and biotechnology.

item.title: Transcription activator-like effector base editing delivered by a targeted lipid nanoparticle for therapy of lung cancer.
item.abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Among them, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all cases, while the mutation of KRAS oncogene plays a crucial role in its formation and metastasis. Here, we report a transcription activator-like effector (TALE) base editor that can accurately identify KRAS gene under the guide of TALE and sgRNA, convert C base to T base, thereby generating a stop codon and blocking the expression of KRAS. Besides, a targeted TALE base editing lipid nanoparticle (targeted TALE LNP) is developed by rationally designing with cancer-targeted EGFR peptide. The targeted TALE LNP exhibits a base editing effect, cancer targeting, and remarkable therapy efficacy in NSCLC cancer-bearing mice. In conclusion, the targeted TALE LNP has the potential to treat lung cancer with KRAS gene mutation through an approach of transcription activator-like effector base editing.

item.title: Engineered live biotherapeutic products: design decisions, failure modes, and clinical translation.
item.abstract: Engineered live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) are viable microorganisms deliberately modified to perform a therapeutic function in a patient. Recombinant therapeutic strains are considered separately from conventional probiotics, donor-derived microbiota products, vaccines, living diagnostics, environmental systems, and systemically administered oncolytic bacteria. Selected oncology platforms share engineering constraints with LBPs, although their classification as LBPs depends on the specific therapy. The target product profile sets the niche, route, and exposure requirements against which chassis, genetic control, and payload release are assessed. Fitness costs, genetic stability, basal leakage, and clearance constrain circuit complexity. Formulation and manufacturing must preserve viability and mechanism-linked potency, with process control and independent containment layers evaluated quantitatively during development. Human studies of engineered metabolic strains support feasibility, short-term tolerability, clearance, and pharmacodynamic activity, although broad or durable clinical benefit has not yet been shown. Microbiota products approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provide regulatory precedents for live microbial medicines, with approval specific to each unengineered product. Clinical trials require separate assessment of target engagement and patient benefit.

item.title: Prokaryotes bridging the lipid divide.
item.abstract: The fundamental biochemical and stereochemical difference in how cell membrane lipids are built between Archaea on one side, and Bacteria and Eukarya on the other is known as the lipid divide. It is often assumed to translate in the impossibility of combining membranes of both types. It was established early when little sampling of the biodiversity was available. Since then, exceptions have been revealed and accumulated. Here, we review those exceptions and complement them with a broad survey, revealing diverse bacteria with mixed membrane-lipid features. Together with liposome assays and synthetic-biology experiments, studies on these organisms suggest that the lipid divide can be bridged. We conclude by discussing the evolutionary implications for LUCA, the origin of the prokaryotic domains and eukaryogenesis.

item.title: Arbitrium crosstalk enables shared signaling among phages.
item.abstract: The arbitrium system has transformed our understanding of phage biology by demonstrating that temperate phages communicate through extracellular peptides to coordinate lysis-lysogeny decisions. Initially considered a highly specific signaling pathway restricted to individual phage lineages, arbitrium communication has now been shown to extend beyond lineage boundaries in some phage systems. Recent studies have shown that non-cognate arbitrium peptides can interact with heterologous receptors, providing evidence of inter-phage crosstalk. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of the molecular basis of arbitrium signaling, the structural determinants of peptide-receptor specificity, and the potential ecological and evolutionary consequences of inter-phage communication. We suggest that arbitrium crosstalk may shape phage ecology by mediating competitive and potentially cooperative interactions within shared signaling environments. We also discuss its potential uses in engineered phage systems, synthetic biology, and microbiome engineering. Collectively, the available evidence broadens the concept of viral communication beyond lineage-specific signaling, while the ecological significance and practical applications of arbitrium crosstalk remain to be established.

item.title: Engineering an Enzymatically Active Granular Matrix for On-Chip Modeling of Bone-Like Mineralization.
item.abstract: Controlled biomineralization is central to engineering physiologically relevant hard-tissue models, yet achieving spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) mineral deposition in microfluidic on-chip systems remains challenging. While cell-based bone-on-chip platforms offer biological complexity, they couple mineral initiation to matrix remodeling and paracrine signaling, complicating isolation of the earliest biochemical drivers of mineralization. Inspired by bottom-up synthetic biology, we engineered an enzymatically active granular matrix that recapitulates a key osteogenic function within a perfusable 3D microenvironment. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP), the key driver of native bone formation, was covalently conjugated to poly(ethylene glycol)-based (PEG) microgels via thiol-ene photochemistry, retaining over 90% of its initial activity after 24 h. These monodisperse microgels were assembled into a jammed, perfusable matrix on-chip, enabling independent control over enzyme loading and substrate delivery. The system supported in situ mineralization (24-48 h), yielding a calcium-deficient, poorly crystalline apatite-like phase characteristic of early-stage bone mineral. We demonstrate 3D localization of enzymatic activity to the granular matrix, which, coupled with interstitial perfusion, enabled mineral formation whose spatial distribution depended on the perfusion regime. This mechanistically defined, acellular platform provides a tunable foundation for investigating ALP-driven 3D mineralization and establishes a modular route toward hybrid biosynthetic models of (patho)physiological tissue mineralization.

item.title: Integrated strategies for enhanced drought tolerance in tomato: from molecular mechanisms to field applications.
item.abstract: Drought stress is a major abiotic constraint on agricultural production, and cultivated tomato varieties are generally sensitive to water deficit. This review systematically summarizes the physiological, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms underlying tomato drought responses. It also integrates recent high-impact insights to advance our understanding of this topic. It then surveys multidimensional improvement strategies. These include biostimulants, chemical regulators, nanomaterials, grafting, water management, and genetic engineering approaches such as transgenesis and CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing. Current research faces bottlenecks in translating laboratory findings to field applications, particularly due to the inherent trade-off between drought tolerance and fruit yield and quality. To address this challenge, we propose a framework that integrates several key components: precision editing tools (e.g. base editing and promoter editing), tissue-specific or stress-inducible expression systems, and parallel phenotyping of yield components and fruit quality traits under both well-watered and drought conditions. This framework is designed to balance stress resilience with productivity. Moving forward, a systematic multidisciplinary approach is required to overcome this trade-off, enabling water-efficient, stable-yielding, and high-quality sustainable tomato production. This review provides an integrative perspective and forward-looking guidance for future research and practical applications.

item.title: Enzymatic preparation of chitin oligosaccharides: Advances in chitinase engineering, synergistic biocatalysis, and process optimization.
item.abstract: Chitin, a linear β-1,4-linked polymer of N-acetyl-d-glucosamine (GlcNAc), is an abundant but recalcitrant polysaccharide. Enzymatic degradation offers a sustainable route to bioactive chitin oligosaccharides (NCOSs), yet faces challenges in yield, specificity, and process efficiency. This review systematically covers chitinase classification, catalytic mechanisms (GH18 retaining vs. GH19 inverting, and LPMO oxidative cleavage), and recent advances in enzyme engineering-including rational design, directed evolution, and synergistic multi-enzyme systems (chitinase + LPMO + GlcNAcase) that significantly enhance saccharification efficiency and modulate product profiles. We also discuss process optimization strategies and emerging computational tools for biocatalyst design as future perspectives. The convergence of these approaches provides a roadmap for the efficient bioconversion of chitin into value-added oligosaccharides for nutraceutical and food applications.

item.title: Bilateral exchange in synthetic biology: experiences, challenges, and opportunities for training and research.
item.abstract: Synthetic biology and the emerging field of biomanufacturing provide new research concepts that should be incorporated into the training of the next generation of scientists. Key elements of synthetic biology are the standardization, modularization, and characterization of biological parts. Defined parts can be assembled into functional transcription units to pathways of multiple units, chromosomes, and/or whole genomes. Here, we highlight the importance of global exchange and state-of-the-art training in the Global South to empower research and reduce the gap between countries. Based on initial seed funding, we established a multidisciplinary bilateral exchange program between Germany and Colombia, including lecture series, experimental workshops, and bilateral exchanges in training and research. The elements are adaptable and our hands-on courses can be carried out with limited resources while covering aspects of synthetic biology. Importantly, this initiative will allow early-career researchers to build an international network, opening up opportunities in research collaboration and paving the way for greater equity.

item.title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
item.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

item.title: Circulating Biomarkers with Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Risk Assessment and Therapeutic Monitoring: Evidence, Limitations, and Translation.
item.abstract: Circulating biomarkers, particularly cell-free DNA (cfDNA), are transforming contemporary medicine through their capacity to provide dynamic, minimally invasive assessments of disease dynamics. Their clinical utility has broadened substantially to include oncology, cardiovascular conditions, transplant monitoring, infectious diseases, and persistent inflammatory disorders. Nevertheless, the increasing complexity and volume of biomarker-related data pose substantial challenges, necessitating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning methodologies for improved data interpretation, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. This review presents a thorough examination of recent progress in the integration of circulating biomarkers with AI within therapeutic contexts and clinical risk management. It outlines the translational trajectory from molecular signatures to precision medicine, addresses present constraints, and explores prospective developments. The objective of this review is to serve as a systematic resource for both clinical practice and research, thereby promoting the evolution of personalized medicine through innovative, biomarker-driven strategies supported by AI.

item.title: Biomaterial-assisted culture of mesenchymal stem cells for enhanced extracellular vesicle production and cartilage regeneration: a systematic review.
item.abstract: Articular cartilage has limited self-repair capacity, prompting interest in cell-free therapies such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This systematic review assessed whether MSCs cultured with biomaterials produce more EVs, and EVs with greater chondrogenic or cartilage-regenerative efficacy, than MSCs in conventional culture. The publications were searched on PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO (2016-2026), and the synthesis of the evidence was done narratively, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From 576 unique records, we included 14 preclinical studies: 12 used biomaterials in a three-dimensional format, and two cultured MSCs on decellularized extracellular matrix. Eleven compared biomaterial-culture EVs head-to-head with conventional-culture EVs for chondrogenic or cartilage-repair outcomes. EV yield was higher with the biomaterial in all ten studies that compared it (about 1.2- to 7.5-fold per cell or per unit of protein). In all 11 comparisons, biomaterial-culture EVs matched or exceeded conventional-culture EVs in chondrocyte proliferation, chondrogenic marker expression, matrix deposition, or in vivo cartilage repair. Cargo-target mechanisms were functionally validated in six studies, although in one the microRNA had been enriched by transfection rather than by the culture platform. Certainty of evidence was low for yield and very low for chondrogenic, cartilage-repair, and anti-inflammatory outcomes. Risk of bias was probably low in seven studies and probably high in seven. The comparator arms often differed in more than the biomaterial, and EV characterization was frequently incomplete. In conclusion, biomaterial-assisted culture is a promising but not yet standardized route to more chondrogenic MSC-derived EVs and requires further study.

item.title: Global profiling of secreted protease activities in Coccidioides posadasii.
item.abstract: Coccidioidomycosis (Valley fever), caused by inhalation of Coccidioides arthroconidia, remains a diagnostic challenge due to its clinical similarity to other respiratory illnesses and the absence of a rapid, definitive diagnostic test. Current approaches, including serology and imaging, often result in delayed or inconclusive diagnosis. Here, we profiled secreted protease activity in cell-free conditioned media from a single strain of Coccidioides posadasii. This activity could potentially form the basis of a protease-targeted diagnostic assay for clinical specimens. Using multiplex substrate profiling by mass spectrometry (MSP-MS) applied to cell-free conditioned media, we characterized global proteolytic activity at acidic (pH 2.5) and neutral (pH 7.4) conditions. At acidic pH, we detected dominant aspartyl protease activity that was inhibited by pepstatin and exhibited substrate preferences similar to human cathepsin D. Consistent with these findings, a commercial cathepsin D fluorogenic substrate was efficiently cleaved under acidic conditions. At neutral pH, we observed distinct proteolytic activity consistent with contributions from both exopeptidases and endopeptidases. Inhibition profiling and fluorogenic substrate assays further suggested involvement of serine and threonine proteases. These findings provide an activity-based characterization of secreted proteases from a single C. posadasii strain and establish a resource for future studies evaluating their biological and diagnostic relevance.

item.title: The Interleukin-33/Growth Stimulation Expressed Gene 2 Signaling Axis in Transplantation: Context-Dependent Roles and Clinical Implications.
item.abstract: This article comprehensively summarizes the expression, mechanisms of action, and clinical significance of the IL-33/ST2 axis in solid organ transplantation and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Rather than being uniformly protective or pathogenic, the IL-33/ST2 axis exerts context-dependent effects: ST2L, expressed on regulatory T cells, group 2 innate lymphoid cells, and Th2 cells, promotes immune tolerance, whereas sST2 acts as a decoy receptor that blocks this pathway and promotes inflammation and fibrosis. The net effect depends on tissue-specific innate immune cell composition, differential ST2 isoform expression, donor versus recipient compartment, intervention timing and dosage, and the degree of ischemia-reperfusion injury. Clinically, elevated sST2 is associated with antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplantation, graft dysfunction in heart transplantation, and treatment-refractory graft-versus-host disease in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, these are primarily observational associations; direct causal evidence from genetic or pharmacological intervention studies remains limited and is often derived from animal models. Comparative analysis across transplant types reveals that sST2 may complement established biomarkers such as donor-derived cell-free DNA and donor-specific antibodies, particularly for chronic graft fibrosis and DSA-negative rejection. Future research should use single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the dynamic expression of ST2 isoforms across immune cells and transplant stages, and explore strategies to induce immune tolerance targeting the IL-33/ST2 axis to improve long-term outcomes for transplant patients.

cards.title_cn: IL-33/ST2 信号轴在移植中的作用：情境依赖效应与临床意义
cards.one_liner: 综述指出 IL-33/ST2 轴在移植中兼具促耐受与促炎双重作用，sST2 可作移植排斥与纤维化的辅助生物标志物。
key_findings: ST2L 表达于 Treg、ILC2 和 Th2 细胞，促进免疫耐受；sST2 作为诱饵受体阻断该通路，促进炎症与纤维化。
净效应取决于组织固有免疫细胞组成、ST2 亚型差异、供受体来源、干预时机剂量及缺血再灌注损伤程度。
临床观察显示 sST2 升高与肾移植抗体介导排斥、心移植移植物功能障碍及难治性 GVHD 相关，但因果证据有限。
cards.why_it_matters: 为移植免疫耐受与慢性纤维化提供新标志物与靶点思路；若从事免疫调控或细胞治疗，可关注 ST2 亚型与单细胞空间转录组方向。

item.title: Graft integration in autologous costal cartilage transplantation: a long-term study using chondrocyte-laden fibrin gel.
item.abstract:
PURPOSE: Mosaicplasty of articular cartilage can be performed using costal cartilage due to its structural similarity. This method has been successfully applied in clinical practice for small joints; however, its use in large joints is limited, partly due to graft displacement. In this study, we used chondrocyte-laden fibrin gel to improve integration in a rat model of autologous costal cartilage transplantation into a knee joint defect and assessed long-term outcomes.
METHODS: Costal cartilage was characterized histologically, immunohistochemically, and biomechanically. Autologous grafts were harvested from the tenth rib and implanted into knee defects pretreated with chondrocyte-laden fibrin gel. Controls included cell-free fibrin gel, defect-only control, and sham-operated animals. Graft integration, subchondral bone resorption, and graft composition were analyzed at 1, 6, and 12 months using micro-CT, histology, and immunostaining.
RESULTS: Costal cartilage demonstrated histological and biomechanical properties comparable to articular cartilage. Chondrocyte-laden fibrin gel did not significantly improve integration but reduced subchondral bone resorption, a preliminary finding consistent with an anti-inflammatory effect. Retained grafts restored joint congruity, integrated with host tissue, and showed no resorption or loss of hyaline cartilage markers over 12 months, despite age-related osteoarthritis changes in surrounding tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: Although chondrocyte-laden fibrin gel did not enhance graft integration, this study demonstrates long-term structural preservation of costal cartilage grafts in a rat knee defect model. Further studies in larger animals are needed to optimize integration strategies and support translation into clinical practice, potentially expanding treatment options for patients with limited donor tissue.

cards.title_cn: 自体肋软骨移植中的移植物整合：载软骨细胞纤维蛋白凝胶的长期研究
cards.one_liner: 载软骨细胞纤维蛋白凝胶未改善大鼠膝关节肋软骨移植物的整合，但减少软骨下骨吸收并维持12个月结构完整。
key_findings: 肋软骨的组织学与生物力学性能与关节软骨相当，适合作为移植材料。
载细胞纤维蛋白凝胶未显著促进整合，但减少了软骨下骨吸收，提示抗炎作用。
12个月内移植物保持关节面一致性、与宿主组织整合，无吸收或透明软骨标志物丢失。
cards.why_it_matters: 为软骨修复提供长期动物实验证据，提示纤维蛋白凝胶的抗炎而非促整合作用，对合成生物学改造支架或递送细胞策略有参考价值。
